intro: A one-story day: Instagram now puts Amazon affiliate links right inside Reels and feed posts. Little else of note.

must_reads.title: Instagram now lets creators add Amazon affiliate links in reels and feed posts
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: up to 30 products per Reel, Amazon tags added automatically even on plain product links, no Instagram cut, and Instagram says in-post links get about 2x the clicks of bio links. Platforms are building affiliate links into the app itself and tying them to one retailer. That changes where creators put links and how much they rely on a link-in-bio, and Geniuslink works across retailers and platforms.

must_reads.title: APMA's new subnetwork code demands publisher-level transparency
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: the UK affiliate trade body now wants every click and sale traced to one named publisher, and wants browser extensions and voucher tools declared. A sign that brands want clearer proof of who drove a sale.

must_reads.title: Reddit pushes logins as Google's AI answers drain its search traffic
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: reports say Reddit traffic is down 13%, partly because of Google's AI Overviews. Even the biggest sites lose clicks when AI answers the question, so fewer shoppers reach the pages where product links sit.

must_reads.title: HarperCollins' TikTok sales are growing. The missing figure is profit
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: big publishers keep selling books inside TikTok, but whether it pays is still unclear. Book sales are spreading across more stores, which is the multi-store world booklinker is built for.

must_reads.title: LinkedIn adds monetization tab to profile analytics
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: LinkedIn is building creator earning tools too. More platforms want creators earning inside them, and each sets its own rules for links.
